question.problem:
Find $y(t)$ given that the Laplace transform of the initial value problem

$$
{y}^{″}(t)-y(t)=-6\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,y(0)=0,\,{y}^{′}(0)=3
$$

is given by

$$
{s}^{2}Y(s)-3-Y(s)=-6(\frac{1}{{s}^{2}+1}).
$$

The solution is $y(t)=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
Using the transformed equation, we can solve for $Y(s)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{s}^{2}Y(s)-3-Y(s) & =-6(\frac{1}{{s}^{2}+1}) \\ ({s}^{2}-1)Y(s) & =3-\frac{6}{{s}^{2}+1} \\ ({s}^{2}-1)Y(s) & =\frac{3({s}^{2}-1)}{{s}^{2}+1} \\ Y(s) & =\frac{3}{{s}^{2}+1}\end{aligned}
$$

which is valid for $s>1.$

Now, taking the inverse Laplace transform, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{L}^{-1}(Y(s)) & ={L}^{-1}\{\frac{3}{{s}^{2}+1}\} \\ y(t) & =3\operatorname{sin}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$
